title: He cried briskly
html_source:
He cried in an energetic and lively voice. Usually used when happy to see someone whom you haven’t spoken to in a long time.

PROPOSED SUGGESTION: Briskness has more to do with being quick than being necessarily lively (although the two obviously go hand-in-hand).

Why would this way of speaking (which is hardly definable with any exactitude) “usually” be used when speaking to someone you haven’t spoken to for a long time? Why this above anything else? How is that relevant to this moment?
